app.title: South Asian Diet Risk Calculator
app.subtitle: Understand your meal's contribution to diabetes and heart disease risk

context.india_description: Risk based on dietary patterns typical in India, where refined cereals and low protein intake are primary drivers (ICMR-INDIAB).
context.us_description: Risk based on dietary patterns of South Asians in the US, where physical inactivity and dietary fat quality are additional documented risk factors (MASALA Study).

scores.heading: Your meal risk scores
scores.band_desc_low: This meal contributes minimally to risk factors.
scores.band_desc_moderate: This meal has notable risk-relevant features.
scores.band_desc_high: This meal meaningfully elevates risk factors.

why_text.high_glycemic_load: The main driver is a high glycemic load — this meal raises blood sugar quickly, which is a primary diabetes risk factor in South Asian populations.
why_text.high_refined_carb_share: A high proportion of the carbohydrates come from refined sources (white rice, maida, or sugar) rather than whole grains.
why_text.low_fiber: This meal is low in dietary fibre, which normally slows digestion and reduces blood sugar spikes after eating.
why_text.poor_protein_quality: Most of the protein comes from sources that do not actively help regulate blood sugar — adding legumes or dairy would improve this.
why_text.high_saturated_fat: The meal is high in saturated fat (likely from ghee, cream, or coconut oil), which raises LDL cholesterol over time.
why_text.poor_fat_quality: The balance of fats leans heavily toward saturated fat. Replacing ghee or coconut oil with mustard oil would improve this.
why_text.high_sodium: Sodium is elevated in this meal, which contributes to blood pressure risk over time.
why_text.none_diabetes: This meal scores well across all diabetes risk factors.
why_text.none_cvd: This meal scores well across all cardiovascular risk factors.

disclaimer.main: These scores are educational tools, not medical diagnoses. Consult a qualified healthcare provider for personal health decisions. Scores reflect a single meal, not your overall dietary pattern.
disclaimer.lpa: Note: approximately 25% of South Asians carry elevated Lp(a) lipoprotein — a genetic cardiovascular risk factor not modifiable by diet and not captured by this score.
disclaimer.visceral_fat: Note: South Asians are predisposed to greater visceral fat accumulation per unit of body weight — a risk factor not fully captured by meal-level scoring.

ml_context.heading: Your personal risk context
ml_context.subtitle: Based on your age, BMI, and activity level — independent of today's meal
ml_context.note: These scores reflect where you sit in the risk distribution of similar South Asians based on population data (NHANES 2011–2018). A higher context score means your baseline risk is elevated — making dietary choices more impactful.
